facts.text: North Capitol Hill once housed Denver's elite in grand Victorian and Queen Anne mansions that later became boarding houses for working‑class families.
By the mid‑20th century, artists and musicians turned the area into a bohemian hub with eclectic shops, cafés, and a Restaurant Row along Seventeenth Avenue.
The Esquire Theatre, originally the Hiawatha Theater opened in 1927, served as Denver's primary art‑house cinema until its July 2024 closure.
North Capitol Hill borders the Colorado State Capitol and Downtown Denver, placing it just east of Broadway and west of City Park.
The neighborhood’s proximity to City Park means residents enjoy easy access to the Denver Zoo and the Museum of Nature & Science.
In the 1950s and 1960s, urban renewal demolished historic structures along East Colfax Avenue, replacing them with commercial developments and modern apartments.
